body.name: refreshed finite-state insulin-policy adaptation
body.construction: Let the state be \(s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) in \(\{50,100,150,200,250\}\times\{0,78\}^2\times\{0,31,850\}^2\times\{0,1\}\), giving \(360\) states. The diet coordinates \((d_1,d_2)\) form \(H_t\); all other coordinates form \(X_t\). Put \(b(1\mid X_t)=0.3\) and \(e(1\mid X_t)=\mathbf 1\{g\ge125\}\). With probability \(1/2\), draw the next full state uniformly. Otherwise draw \(d_0\in\{0,78\}\) with probabilities \((0.8,0.2)\), draw \(x_0\in\{0,31,850\}\) with probabilities \((0.4,0.4,0.2)\), draw \(\xi\sim N(0,25)\), set \(g'=\operatorname{round}_{\{50,100,150,200,250\}}\operatorname{clip}_{[50,250]}(10+0.9g+0.1d_1+0.1d_2-0.01x_1-0.01x_2-2A_t-4a_1+\xi)\), and shift the memories to \((g',d_0,d_1,x_0,x_1,A_t)\). Set \(Y_t=-1\) for \(g\le70\), \(Y_t=-2/3\) for \(g>150\), \(Y_t=-1/3\) for \(70<g\le80\) or \(120<g\le150\), and \(Y_t=0\) otherwise. This defines \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\).
